spec.description: Left column is absolute values, right column is the differentials and rates. Keep new panels in that order.

spec.expr: max(last_over_time({service="cardano-node", kind="LeiosAnnouncementAccepted", instance=~"$instance"} | label_format ts=`{{ __timestamp__.UnixMilli }}` | unwrap ts [1h]))
max(last_over_time({service="cardano-node", kind="LeiosValidClaim", instance=~"$instance"} | label_format ts=`{{ __timestamp__.UnixMilli }}` | unwrap ts [1h]))

spec.description:
Time since any producer's announcement was accepted (LeiosAnnouncementAccepted, from any source) and since a CertRB's certificate verified in chain selection (LeiosValidClaim). Each is the latest across our nodes, so it falls to zero at every announcement or certificate and climbs in between.

To see where our own nodes announced or certified, turn on the "Show our Leios announcements" and "Show our Leios certifications" toggles at the top.

LeiosValidClaim is a Debug trace under ChainDB.AddBlockEvent.AddBlockLeiosEvent; without that severity the certification line stays empty.
spec.title: Time since last Leios certification or announcement

spec.expr: avg_over_time({service="cardano-node/leios-voting", instance=~"$instance", kind="LeiosEbValidated"} | json | label_format hit=`{{ divf .reapplied (addf .reapplied .applied) }}` | unwrap hit [${window}s]) by (instance)

spec.description:
Cache hit rate when the voting thread validates an EB's closure to decide whether to vote for it -- not the apply path that runs when a certified EB's closure is applied to the chain. Of the txs in the closure, the share the LeiosTxCache spared full validation: reapplied means the cache had already validated the tx, so only the state-dependent checks re-ran; applied means it was validated from scratch. Plotted as reapplied / (reapplied + applied).

The ratio is computed per validation and then averaged over the Rate / avg window, so every validation in the window contributes equally whatever its closure size. Narrow the window to see individual validations; widen it to see the trend. 0 and 1 are common and real: a closure is often entirely cached or entirely fresh.

Per node, since nodes do not see the same announcement at the same time and a fleet aggregate would average over different EB sets. Narrow with the instance variable, or click a legend entry to isolate a node.

A high hit rate does not imply cheap validation -- reapplyTx runs per tx either way, so validation cost tracks closure size, not this ratio. This is also the work that sits inside the vote window, so it is the cost that can make a vote too late.

Gaps are windows in which that node validated nothing.

The panel below measures the same thing weighted by transaction instead of by validation, from counters rather than a log scan. The two answer different questions and are shown together deliberately.
spec.title: Cache hit rate for voting EB validation, per node

spec.description:
The same cache hit rate as the panel above, weighted by transaction rather than by validation. That one averages a ratio computed per validation, so every validation counts equally whatever its closure size; this one divides two counters, so every transaction counts equally.

They will not agree, and neither is wrong. A node validating many small cached closures and one large fresh one reads higher above. Weighting by validation answers how often a closure was cached; weighting by transaction answers what share of the work the cache spared. Which is the useful question is a call for whoever is tuning the cache.

This form is a Mimir query rather than a log scan, so it is roughly an order of magnitude cheaper and stays cheap as the fleet grows. What it cannot show is the per-validation spread: the 0 and 1 readings visible above are real, and that texture does not survive aggregation into counters.

Counters come from leios_diffusion_process, so this panel is blank on any deployment without that module.
spec.title: Cache hit rate, counter-based (weighted by tx, not by validation)

spec.expr: avg_over_time({service="cardano-node", kind="LeiosAdaptiveEb", instance=~"$instance"} | json v="participation", c="certifiable" | c="true" | unwrap v [${window}s]) by (instance)
avg_over_time({service="cardano-node", kind="LeiosAdaptiveEb", instance=~"$instance"} | json v="ebCapacityScale" | unwrap v [${window}s]) by (instance)

avg_over_time({service="cardano-node", kind="LeiosAdaptiveEb", instance=~"$instance"} | json m="missedQuorum", c="certifiable" | c="true", m!="" | label_format miss=`{{ if eq .m "true" }}1{{ else }}0{{ end }}` | unwrap miss [${window}s]) by (instance)

spec.description:
Each producer's adaptive endorsements controller (LeiosAdaptiveEb), averaged over the Rate / avg window. Only certifiable announcements count.

Voted is the stake that voted on an announcement, against the quorum threshold (red line). The controller's input on the right axis is the share of them that missed it. Each miss cuts the capacity scale by Decrease (0.8), each quorum made adds Increase (0.01) back, down to MinScale.
spec.title: Adaptive endorsements

spec.expr: avg_over_time({service="cardano-node", kind="LeiosBlockForged", instance=~"$instance"} | json txs="numTxs" | unwrap txs [${window}s]) by (instance)
avg_over_time({service="cardano-node", kind="LeiosAdaptiveEb", instance=~"$instance"} | json scale="ebCapacityScale" | unwrap scale [${window}s]) by (instance)

spec.description:
Transactions per forged endorser block, per node, averaged over the Rate / avg window.

Read the shape, not the level: a flat top means a size limit is binding, while scatter below the ceiling means the forge time budget is. The red line is the hard per-EB transaction cap, which no protocol parameter can raise.

Dashed lines on the right axis are each producer's adaptive endorsements capacity scale (LeiosAdaptiveEb). Where a producer has it enabled, the fill should track its scale: the EB capacity is cut to that share after announcements miss their quorum. See the Adaptive endorsements panel for why.
spec.title: Endorser block fill
